title: Two threats, one move
intro: A fork attacks two pieces at once. Find a knight move that checks the king and attacks another piece.
tip: Look at every square your knight can jump to.

p.text: Check the king on e7 and attack the queen on f6. After the king moves, take the queen.
Check the king on g8 and attack the rook on h7. The king threat must be answered first.
Check the king on e8 while attacking the queen on b7. Knights can jump over pieces.

title: The piece that cannot move
intro: A pin traps a piece in front of its king. Capture the pinned knight with your bishop.
tip: Trace the line from your rook to the enemy king.

p.text: The rook pins the knight on e7 to the king on e8. Capture with the bishop. The king cannot recapture onto the rook’s line.
The knight cannot leave the d-file without exposing its king. Capture it with the bishop.
The rook pins the knight to its king along the f-file. Capture the knight with your bishop.

title: Close every escape square
intro: Checkmate means the king is in check with no legal escape. Find mate in one move.
tip: After a check, ask: can the king move, capture, or block?

p.text: The rook checks along the back rank. The king’s pawns block its escape. Nothing can block or capture the rook.
The rook checks the eighth rank and covers g8. The pawns block g7 and h7.
The queen checks and covers every escape. Your king protects the queen, so the enemy king cannot capture it.

title: Think one reply ahead
intro: Give a rook check that also attacks the queen. Picture the king moving away, then your rook taking the queen.
tip: Think: my move, their reply, my next move.

p.text: Check along the eighth rank and attack the queen on a8. The king must move off the rank; then capture the queen.
The rook checks the king and attacks the queen. After the king leaves the eighth rank, take the queen on a8.
Check first. The king must leave the eighth rank, then your rook can take the queen on a8.
